subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should this race be fixed with a narrow locked/current-file merge for allow-always and usage writes, or folded into the broader guarded exec-approvals state repair tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78225 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226?
rationale: Both paths touch persisted exec approval security state, and the open broader PR is currently conflicting with unresolved review concerns, so automation should not choose the permanent security-state write contract alone.

options.title: Use one guarded exec-approvals store repair
options.body: Adopt or replace the broader guarded-write approach so allow-always additions, usage metadata, and admin policy changes share one freshness rule.

options.title: Land a narrow allow-always race fix first
options.body: Fix only concurrent allow-always and usage writes now, while keeping the stale admin writeback issue open for a separate reviewed security patch.

options.title: Defer to a larger storage redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide whether exec approvals should move away from JSON full-file writes entirely.

recommendation.title: Use one guarded exec-approvals store repair
recommendation.body: Adopt or replace the broader guarded-write approach so allow-always additions, usage metadata, and admin policy changes share one freshness rule.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal across the exec approval implementation and security hardening commits.
